title: Careful governance is needed to balance the benefits and risks of landfill mining in China | Science
description: In recent years, dozens of Chinese cities across the Yangtze and Pearl River deltas have launched large-scale landfill mining, a process that entails sealed, decades-old municipal waste landfills being excavated and their contents being sorted and combusted in waste-to-energy plants (1, 2). Driven by shrinking fresh combustible waste after mandatory waste classification and overbuilt incineration capacity, this emerging practice delivers tangible socioeconomic and environmental gains yet carries overlooked ecological risks that demand balanced governance (3).
